chunks: Al-Halabi narrated from Abu Abdullah, from his father, peace be upon them:

That when he would go out on the day of al-Fitr and al-Adha, he refused to have a carpet brought for him to pray upon. He would say: “This is a day on which the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, would go out until he was exposed to the horizons of the sky, then he would place his forehead upon the earth.”

key_terms.آفَاقِ السَّمَاءِ: the open horizons of the sky, indicating an uncovered outdoor place
key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the earth or ground, upon which the sajdah was made
key_terms.الْأَضْحَى: Eid al-Adha, the festival of sacrifice
key_terms.الْفِطْرِ: Eid al-Fitr, the festival marking the end of sawm
key_terms.بِطِنْفِسَةٍ: a carpet or mat brought for praying on
key_terms.جَبْهَتَهُ: his forehead, the part placed on the earth in sajdah
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: How did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and the Imams عليهم السلام perform the Eid prayer area practice regarding سجدة on the earth?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the practice of the Imam عليه السلام on the days of Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha, refusing a carpet for prayer and praying directly upon the earth. It presents this as following the sunnah of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in going out openly and placing his forehead on the ground.
